title: Canonicalize benchmark runtime lockfile and runner contracts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our token/sec and p95 benchmarking results have significant variance between runs that appears correlated with subtle differences in driver versions, CUDA/cuDNN stacks, and ephemeral runner images used in CI. This makes regression detection noisy and increases investigation time for apparently failing performance checks. Goal: produce a single canonical 'benchmark runtime lockfile' and a minimal runner contract (runtime interface + required utilities) that all benchmark harnesses (local, CI, nightly, and perf-lab) must use. This ticket covers spec, validation, CI enforcement, and migration steps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single canonical lockfile (driver+CUDA+cuDNN+base-image tags) committed to repo (benchmarks/benchmark-lockfile.txt). 2) Benchmark runner contract v1 documented and implemented: required kernel flags, pinned python/torch-cu wheel tags, nvidia-container-toolkit configuration, and /dev/nv* access rules. 3) CI validator job that fails build if benchmark runs don't use the lockfile (unit test + dry-run). 4) Nightly regression job that runs matrix and posts tokens/sec and p95 metrics to perf dashboard. 5) <10% variance on repeated benchmark runs (after warmup) across identical hardware environments.
plan: Phase 1: Audit current benchmark environments and collect metadata from last 30 perf runs (driver, CUDA, image, runner commit). Phase 2: Propose canonical lockfile entries and runner contract; review with kernel/runtime teams and infra. Phase 3: Implement lockfile enforcement in CI (bench-ci-validate) and update local runner images and bench lab. Phase 4: Run 2-week shadow run to measure variance improvement and tune warmup/kv-cache seeding. Phase 5: Roll out to all benchmark pipelines and add automatic regression alerts.
metrics_and_targets: Primary: tokens/sec (throughput) and p95 (latency) per model/seq_len. Targets: baseline tokens/sec +-5% across repeated runs on same physical GPU; p95 regression alerts if >10% degradation vs moving baseline. Secondary: CI flakiness rate for benchmark jobs <1% over 30 days.
implementation_notes: - Lockfile format: newline entries 'component==version' style (e.g., nvidia-driver==535.86, cuda==12.2, cudnn==8.9.2, base-image==gcr.io/redwood/bench:2026-01-12). - Runner contract v1: entrypoint script path, required ENV vars (NV_VISIBLE_DEVICES, BENCHMARK_GID), kernel module checks, mandatory /etc/nvidia-container-runtime/config.toml keys. - Warmup: 3 warmup runs of 64 tokens, then 5 measured runs. - KV cache state: benchmarks must declare 'kv_empty' or 'kv_warmed' and the lockfile must include an optional seed-data tag.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Pinning older drivers could prevent using latest performance fixes. Mitigation: Maintain a peri-month driver refresh cadence and a compatibility matrix in the lockfile with 'primary' and 'fallback' entries. Risk: Runner contract too restrictive breaks ad-hoc experiments. Mitigation: Keep a documented 'experimental' runner flow and allow overrides only in non-CI lab clusters.
example_commands:
# validate local runner uses lockfile
python bench/validate_lockfile.py --lockfile benchmarks/benchmark-lockfile.txt

# run single benchmark with runner contract enforced
docker run --gpus all --env-file bench/env.list --entrypoint /bench/run_benchmark.sh gcr.io/redwood/bench:2026-01-12 --model llama-7b --seq-len 512 --measure p95,tokens_per_sec
migration_steps: 1) Merge lockfile PR and land CI validator. 2) Update bench images in perf-lab and the dev bench image tags. 3) Run a canary suite on 3 GPU nodes (A100,H100) and collect metrics for 48 hours. 4) If variance reduction > 30% vs baseline, promote to nightly pipelines. 5) Communicate rollout to teams and add a deprecation window for legacy runner images.
